newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 6.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Irish prime minister John Bruton accused Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams of issuing a menacing reminder that the IRA has not gone away.
- Dubliner Ken Doherty became the first world snooker champion from the Republic of Ireland when he beat Scotland's Stephen Hendry by 18 frames to 12 in the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield last night.
- Ireland's biggest mortgage lender Irish Permanent Plc is expected to kick off a round of interest rate hikes on Tuesday, announcing an increase of a half of one percentage point in its rates.
- The row over water charges escalated last night when the European Union signalled its anger at their abolition by proposing a five percent cut in grant aid for Irish water schemes.
- U.S. company Netscape is to set up an operation in Dublin employing up to 100 people initially.
- Ken Doherty was crowned snooker's world champion last night, winning a first prize of 210,000 pounds and the chance to make more than one million in the next twelve months.
- A bank holiday crowd watched in horror yesterday as desperate efforts failed to save a man washed overboard from a yacht off Clogherhead, County Louth.
- Justice minister Nora Owen turned the election spotlight on crime when she rounded on the opposition for failing to tackle the so-called revolving door prison system while in government.
- The government will today launch a desperate bid to re-open Middle Eastern cattle export markets worth over 300 million and bolster collapsing beef prices.
- Ireland rose to its feet and roared as 27-year old Dubliner Ken Doherty became the first man from the Republic to become world snooker champion.
